verdict.root_cause: At 09:49:07 UTC an automated environment-variable update (actor 'platform-automation') repointed cartservice's Redis backing address to the redis-cart host on port 6380 (tr_afbf7ec16980). Nothing listening usable is reachable at that endpoint: cartservice's own logs show repeated connect attempts to redis-cart:6380 with TLS disabled, each ending in a connect failure raised out of RedisCartStore.InitializeAsync/EnsureRedisConnected as an unhandled exception from Program.Main, putting the process into a crash/restart loop from ~09:52:36 through 09:55:20 (tr_4ebe4ee16310). Because cartservice dies during initialization it never serves cart RPCs, so every checkout trace fails at the same point: the CartService GetCart child span under prepareOrderItemsAndShippingQuoteFromCart is the deepest span carrying ERROR and the error propagates up through checkoutservice and frontend (tr_df9a68fd96ac). checkoutservice itself is blameless — no change is recorded for it in the onset window (tr_5d1f4532b2a4) and its local order-assembly span is consistently non-error (tr_df9a68fd96ac). The failing value is the endpoint itself: a wrong port in a configuration string is what breaks every request, so the misconfiguration is the mechanism, not merely an upstream act.
verdict.reasoning: Three independent lines converge on the cart-fetch step. Traces localise the fault precisely: the GetCart child span is the deepest ERROR span and no paymentservice/currencyservice/accountingservice/emailservice spans appear at all, so checkout aborts before those calls — which also rules out the four unmeasured edges triage flagged (tr_df9a68fd96ac). checkoutservice logs corroborate the shape from the caller's side: after 09:51 orders are accepted but no payment, email, or message-write completion lines follow, and no error line names a dependency — a stall/abort at or before payment, consistent with a failing cart lookup rather than checkout-internal logic (tr_6a5141eb5726). cartservice logs then supply the mechanism and the endpoint: connect-stage failures against redis-cart:6380, in the startup path, terminating the process repeatedly (tr_4ebe4ee16310); the same host:port appears verbatim in the only recorded change to cartservice in the window, applied ~2.5 minutes before the 09:51:45 page (tr_afbf7ec16980). Timing, endpoint identity, and failure stage all line up. Classification: not dependency_latency — traces are 1–4ms end-to-end with sub-millisecond GetCart spans, so this is fast failure, not waiting (tr_df9a68fd96ac). Not resource_exhaustion — no capacity, max-clients, eviction, or pool-exhaustion signals, and one connect attempt per process start fails outright (tr_4ebe4ee16310). Not bad_deploy — no image or version rollout is recorded for cartservice, only an environment mutation (tr_afbf7ec16980). Remediation is config_revert rather than restart: the crash loop already restarts the process every ~20–40s and it fails identically each time, so restarting cannot help while the address remains wrong. The corpus entry cart-bad-image-tag is a useful caution here — the empty cartservice metric series (tr_97b723431be4) must not be read as 'cart is healthy'; the specialist correctly notes the unfiltered denominator is empty too, which is a missing-series condition, not a clean bill of health.
open_questions: Is 6380 actually wrong, or is redis-cart genuinely meant to listen there (e.g. a TLS port) while cartservice connects with TLS disabled? The logs show TLS disabled against a non-default port (tr_4ebe4ee16310); reverting to 6379 versus enabling TLS on 6380 are different fixes and the evidence does not distinguish them.

The change log records no prior value for the Redis address (tr_afbf7ec16980), so the correct value to revert to is not established by evidence and must be read from a known-good manifest or a peer environment.

Why did checkoutservice's error ratio peak at ~67% with intervals returning to zero (tr_96fdfcc4f20e) while all ~40 sampled traces showed a uniform failure pattern (tr_df9a68fd96ac)? Possible low-denominator sampling artifact, or partial success during cartservice's brief pre-crash windows — unresolved; call volume was never retrieved.

The exact onset is unpinned. cartservice was healthy at ~09:41:47 and first observed failing at 09:52:36 (tr_4ebe4ee16310), while checkoutservice logs are missing roughly 09:42–09:51 (tr_6a5141eb5726). Whether failures began immediately at the 09:49:07 change or after a delay (cache TTL, pod restart schedule) is not settled.

cartservice has no calls_total series at all (tr_97b723431be4). Whether this is a pre-existing instrumentation/label gap or a symptom of the crash loop is unknown, and it left the saturation question entirely unanswered.

Scope of the automated change: triage counted 12 affected services, but only cartservice's change log was queried. Whether platform-automation applied the same endpoint edit to other services sharing this Redis is unverified, as is what triggered the automation.
checkoutservice's change coverage is only ~15 minutes and scoped to itself (tr_5d1f4532b2a4); a change landing between 08:51 and 09:41, or on another dependency, is outside what was checked.
